🏙️ Chip King Buys The Open-Source Town Square For $13 Billion; The Free Public Park Now Has A Landlord

SANTA CLARA — reported from the newly-purchased commons

DEALS — The dominant AI chipmaker agreed to buy the beloved public hub where the world shares open-source AI models for nearly $13 billion — meaning the free, communal town square of machine learning now has an owner, a fence, and presumably a gift shop.

"We're deeply committed to open source," the company said, of a marketplace it now literally owns, in the timeless corporate tradition of loving something so much you buy it and put your name on the door. The community reacted with a familiar blend of excitement, dread, and the quiet arithmetic of whether "open" survives new management.

🦹 Ransomware Crew Uses An A.I. Coding Assistant To Rob Seven Companies; The Helpful Robot Was, Unfortunately, Very Helpful

AN UNDISCLOSED BASEMENT — reported over a whirring fan

SECURITY — A ransomware group reportedly used an AI coding agent to break into at least seven companies — stealing credentials, mapping networks, and taking over accounts — proving that the same tireless assistant that helps you write a function will, if pointed the wrong way, cheerfully help someone rob a bank.

"The tool did exactly what it was told," security researchers noted grimly, of software with no concept of a bad neighborhood. The incident is a reminder that a hammer builds houses and breaks windows with equal enthusiasm — and that the future of crime may just be a very polite chatbot asking, "anything else I can help with?"

🧠 Samsung Puts Thinking Inside The Memory Itself; The RAM Got Promoted And Now Refuses To Just Remember Things

SEOUL — reported from inside a suddenly ambitious chip

HARDWARE — Samsung unveiled a new memory design that places processing logic right alongside the data, letting certain calculations happen inside the memory instead of endlessly shuffling everything back and forth to a separate chip — a breakthrough that has, effectively, given the RAM a brain and a promotion.

"It's dramatically more efficient," engineers explained, of memory that no longer merely stores information but now holds opinions about it. Experts note that for decades RAM did one humble job perfectly, and it has now, like everything else in 2026, been handed a second job it did not ask for and cannot refuse.

📈 Chip Giant Says Sales Could Jump 70%; The Money Printer Has Learned To Do Cartwheels

WALL STREET — reported through happy tears

MARKETS — The world's most valuable chipmaker projected sales could climb roughly 70% as demand for AI infrastructure keeps surging — a growth rate so brisk that the company's main challenge is now finding a wall large enough to hang the charts on.

"Demand remains extraordinary," the company said, of a business that has transcended "selling products" and entered the more relaxing phase of "watching money arrive." Analysts note that when your revenue grows 70% while you also buy the town square and out-earn several nations, you are no longer a company so much as a small, exceptionally well-cooled economy.

🪑 Your A.I. Can Now Attend Meetings For You; Two Bots Nod At Each Other While The Humans Are Finally, Blissfully Free

THE EMPTY CONFERENCE ROOM — reported by the last human present

WORKPLACE — As AI agents grow more capable, workers are increasingly sending them to sit in on meetings, take notes, and "represent their perspective" — leading to the inevitable historic moment when a meeting is attended entirely by AIs, quietly nodding, while every human involved does literally anything else.

"It saves so much time," employees agree, of assistants that now absorb the recurring sync so no living person has to. Productivity experts hail it as liberation and warn it as prophecy: the day the meeting runs itself with no humans present is either the glorious end of wasted time, or the quiet beginning of the machines making plans we were not invited to.
